verdict.rationale: Proton Pass ships an official CLI that is explicitly positioned for retrieving secrets across scripts, deployments, and CI/CD pipelines, with CRUD over vaults and items. So the product itself provides a headless automation surface. The evidence is a single launch blog post. It does not document non-interactive authentication for CI (service accounts, access tokens, or env-var login) or any working pipeline integration, so the depth of headless operation is unproven. missing for 10: documented non-interactive/headless authentication for CI runners, concrete CI integration docs or examples, independent or hands-on corroboration of CLI use in automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: the CLI enables you to securely retrieve secrets and other items across scripts, deployments, and continuous integration/ continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines.
Create, read, update, and delete vaults
View, create, update, and delete items including passwords, secure notes, credit cards, identities, WiFi entries, custom items, and stored SSH-key items
